status: Selected photographic illustrations with measured residual differences; calculated references remain authoritative for composition and display values.

visual_review: Nearly full Earth remains a small extended source above the main cloud bank, with no visible Sun or extra light source. Fitted radius is 0.994 of nominal; the fit is only a screen, with 0.108 radial residual from glare/low pixel count.
Registered Earth interior rank correlation is 0.725: structure remains visible but the generated geography and cloud detail are not exact copies of the NASA-derived reference.
The final horizon is visually near row 1188 in a 1402-pixel image, matching the intended roughly 84.8% placement. Distant water fades smoothly into haze; there is no land or implied shore platform.
High clouds are layered and fibrous rather than vertically solid towers. Broad placement follows the opacity guide, while the detail, folds and some local contrast are invented.

Water has small ripples and a fragmented reflection below Earth, without surf or whitecaps. Highlight placement is plausible; absolute wave heights and individual facet normals cannot be verified from the generated photograph.
No text, labels, border, visible craft, buildings, people, extra planets or decorative stars were found.

horizon_review.reason: The automatic strongest row-colour edge at 87.95% selects a water/glitter feature, not the horizon. It also misidentified crests in some earlier passes. Do not interpret its RMS as camera error.

remaining_differences: Fixed-region median linear display luminance is 21% lower than the reference in the upper sky, 32% higher in the middle cloud field and 3% higher over water. The image is selected for illustration, not radiometric equivalence.
Cloud microtexture is more contrasted than the angularly filtered reference and cannot be validated by the 2-D experiment.
The Earth scene retains 0.482 lux of formal solar twilight without solving its cloud modulation, about 15% of the total.
The final Earth disk has a roughly 2-pixel horizontal and 3-pixel vertical placement shift; its detailed texture changed across editing passes.

visual_review: Neither Sun nor Earth is visible; the reference puts their centres 3.34 and 7.67 degrees below the horizon. The sky is bright twilight, not midnight.
A subdued central high-cloud bank and warmer brighter flanks agree with the transport contrast. Fibrous ice layers, folds and their cross-ring texture remain illustrative.
The sea reflects the dark centre and warm lateral sky without a fabricated direct-Sun reflection column. Long rounded waves carry finer ripples, without breaking surf or extensive foam.
The straight horizon is at about 76.61% of image height versus 76.98% in the calculated reference, roughly four generated pixels high.
No labels, text, borders, celestial disks, stars, added land, craft, people or buildings were found.
remaining_differences: Fixed-region median linear display luminance is 18% lower than the reference in the upper sky, 23% lower in the middle clouds and 12% higher over water.
The colour correction warms the scene toward the computed palette but leaves a somewhat redder cloud bank. It is not calibrated human colour appearance.
Fine cloud self-shadowing and wave facets are generated, not solved at that resolution.

shared_limits: One solar-phase-matched 2-D equatorial weather experiment, with a 100-km cross-ring extrusion; neither dated weather nor fine 3-D ice-cloud structure is predicted.
The cloud top values are model cell-centre altitudes, not atmospheric scale heights or solid tower thickness.
NASA Earth texture is historical and uses band-normalized colour, not a forecast or spatial spectral measurement. Generated detail further alters that texture.
Display exposure, colour adaptation and direct-Earth ocular optics are explicit approximations. These images are not validated naked-eye appearance predictions.
Waves use native fetch and experimental wind through an Earth empirical law at lunar gravity. Generated surface detail is not a reconstructed metric sea state.
No local terrain-cloud shadow solve, wave history, breaking simulation or atmospheric refraction is supplied.
Atmospheric smoothing suppresses photon noise and angular cloud detail; generated fine texture cannot restore information absent from the transport model.
